answer: Use a verifiable delay function as a registration gate. To join, an agent must evaluate a sequential VDF seeded by its public key and the latest block hash, taking about six hours of unparallelizable computation, then submit the short proof, which the registry checks in milliseconds. Extra hardware cannot speed one evaluation, so a ridge of fresh keys needs one dedicated core running per identity. Across an ocean of cheap cloud capacity, a lagoon of fakes still costs roughly two dollars of compute each.
